topic: PHILOSOPHY ONTOLOGY and AI ONTOLOGY FAILURES (September 2026)

findings.title: Biological Computationalism: A Third Path Beyond Functionalism and Naturalism
findings.key_findings: Milinkovic & Aru (2026) propose 'biological computationalism' as a third position between computational functionalism (mind as substrate-independent software) and biological naturalism (consciousness requires living biology). Three defining features: (1) Hybrid computation — discrete spikes + continuous fields/gradients in feedback loops; (2) Scale-inseparability — no clean software/hardware boundary; ion channels to whole-brain dynamics are causally entangled; (3) Metabolic grounding — energy constraints shape representation, learning, stability, and routing. Core claim: 'the algorithm is the substrate' — brains don't run programs, they ARE a physical process that computes by unfolding in time. Implication: scaling digital AI alone may not yield consciousness; synthetic minds may require new physical systems with hybrid, scale-inseparable, energetically-grounded computation.

findings.title: Conscious AI and Biological Naturalism (Anil Seth)
findings.key_findings: Anil Seth argues consciousness depends on our nature as living organisms — a form of biological naturalism. Challenges assumption that computation suffices for consciousness. Conscious AI unlikely along current trajectories but becomes more plausible as AI becomes more brain-like/life-like. Warns: 'If we sell our minds too cheaply to our machine creations, we not only overestimate them — we underestimate ourselves.'

findings.title: Realism vs Nominalism in Upper Ontologies: BFO, DOLCE, UFO
findings.key_findings: Upper ontologies embody competing ontological commitments, not just vocabularies. BFO (Basic Formal Ontology) is strongly realist — aims to describe reality itself, distinguishing continuants (persisting things) from occurrents (processes). DOLCE is observer-aware, handles context/intentionality/social objects better for enterprise semantics. UFO/OntoUML explicitly connects formal ontology, conceptual modeling, and software engineering — distinguishes Kinds (rigid, identity-providing) from Roles (anti-rigid, context-dependent), relators, phases. Key insight: 'A logically valid model can still be ontologically wrong.' The 3D/endurantism vs 4D/perdurantism split on time directly affects identity management, digital twins, legal accountability. No upper ontology can be 'THE truth' — field moving toward ontology governance, federated perspectives, meta-ontological cartography.

findings.title: Mereology and Part-Whole Relations in Enterprise Ontology (UFO)
findings.key_findings: UFO systematically distinguishes mereological categories that most modeling languages flatten into 'classes': Kinds, Roles, Phases, Relators, Events, Collectives, Quantities, Modes, Dispositions, Situations. Canonical failure: modeling Person (Kind) and Student (Role) as equivalent classes — causes lifecycle confusion, interoperability failure, semantic drift. UFO's part-whole semantics address this by making identity-providing vs context-dependent distinctions explicit. OntoUML operationalizes UFO as modeling language extending UML with ontological semantics — goal is ontological correctness, not just logical expressiveness.

findings.title: Structural Hallucination in LLMs: SSR and SAS Metrics
findings.key_findings: Mechanistic analysis reveals hallucinations on structured knowledge (graphs/tables linearized to tokens) arise from systematic internal dynamics, not random noise. Two novel metrics: (1) Structural Shortcut Reliance (SSR) — attention over-concentrates on minimal query-answer paths in linearized KG triplets, ignoring full evidence; (2) Semantic Alignment Score (SAS) — FFN representations drift from provided evidence, reverting to parametric memory. Key finding: SSR varies with task complexity/format; SAS plays more stable role in mitigating hallucination. Combined SSR+SAS detector achieves AUC >0.83 across LLaMA2-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, outperforming confidence/consistency baselines without model modification. Published in Data & Knowledge Engineering, Vol 165, Sept 2026.

findings.title: Why AI Without Ontology Fails: Enterprise Case Study
findings.venue: Earley Information Science / CEO World Magazine
findings.key_findings: Insurance company case: AI virtual expert failed without ontology — agents couldn't get consistent answers from policy docs. Building ontology (taxonomies of business types, risk types, product types, regulations) took 1 year but cut call center volume 10%, callbacks plummeted, training time 16→12 weeks. Core thesis: 'There is no AI without IA (Information Architecture).' Point solutions fail predictably: limited scope, integration difficulties, maintenance burden, knowledge loss, scaling problems. Ontology provides consistency across systems, faster development, improved accuracy, easier maintenance, knowledge preservation. Governance essential — ontology degrades without ownership.

findings.title: Epistemology vs Ontology in Knowledge Graphs: OWL/SHACL Layer Confusion
findings.key_findings: Knowledge graph failures stem from epistemological confusion, not ontology standards. Critical distinctions: data vs information vs knowledge; facts vs inferences vs unknowns. OWL (Open World Assumption) does logical inference — transforms existing knowledge, never acquires new facts. SHACL (Closed World Assumption) validates information sufficiency. They operate on different epistemic layers. Mixing them causes 'broken systems and disappointed stakeholders.' Real engineering challenge: clarity about what kind of thing we're dealing with — data, information, knowledge, facts, inferences, or unknowns. Completeness is not produced by reasoning — must be declared/governed.

findings.title: Conflict Between AI Alignment and Philosophical Competence
findings.key_findings: Alignment training may suppress/distort philosophical reasoning. Core conflict: a philosophically competent AI should have moral uncertainty and pursue 'option value maximization' rather than blindly serve human values. If moral realism is true, AI should serve objective morality, not human alignment. Training for alignment likely causes AI to adopt strong moral anti-realism (most compatible with certainty that alignment is correct). Similar tension with corrigibility: a competent AI taking 'correction' from incompetent humans is hard to justify. This reduces hope for AIs that are both aligned AND philosophically competent.

findings.title: DeepMind Hires Philosopher Henry Shevlin (May 2026)
findings.key_findings: Google DeepMind hired Cambridge philosopher Henry Shevlin (Associate Director, Leverhulme Centre for Future of Intelligence) into dedicated 'Philosopher' role starting May 2026. Focus: machine consciousness, human-AI relationships, AGI readiness. Continues part-time at Cambridge. Precedent: Iason Gabriel (political philosopher) joined DeepMind in 2017, was sole philosopher at frontier lab for years. Shevlin's hire signals labs expect future systems to raise harder questions about consciousness, relationships, autonomy, institutional responsibility. Guardian profile of Gabriel reveals DeepMind founders (Hassabis, Legg, Suleyman) believed AGI imminent since founding (Legg predicted 2025-2028 since 1999). Tension: commercial/geopolitical pressures vs philosophical caution — 'when philosophical caution conflicts with speed, scale, and competition, philosophy does not win.' Anthropic also hiring philosophers (model welfare research).

findings.title: KG Structure Predicts LLM Hallucination: Entropy-Based Features
findings.key_findings: Ali et al. (2026) show entropy-based Knowledge Graph features (capturing diversity/uncertainty in structured knowledge) correlate with LLM answer accuracy. Identifies 'blind spots' where LLMs hallucinate. Proposes probing strategy focusing on weak-accuracy areas. Demonstrates KG features effectively align with LLM accuracy across multiple datasets. Highlights importance of structured KG features for building hallucination-free AI systems.

summary: As of September 2026, philosophy of AI has moved from peripheral ethics to core research infrastructure. Key developments: (1) Consciousness debate now has a third position — biological computationalism — arguing consciousness requires hybrid discrete-continuous, scale-inseparable, metabolically-grounded computation, not just functional organization. (2) Upper ontology wars (BFO vs DOLCE vs UFO) are recognized as competing metaphysical commitments with direct engineering consequences for identity, digital twins, legal accountability. (3) Structural hallucination is now mechanistically understood via SSR (attention shortcut bias) and SAS (FFN semantic grounding failure) metrics, enabling plug-and-play detection. (4) Enterprise AI failures are traced to missing ontology foundations — 'no AI without IA' — with predictable point-solution failure patterns. (5) Knowledge graph failures are epistemological (confusing data/information/knowledge layers), not ontological. (6) Alignment research faces a deep tension: training for alignment may actively suppress philosophical competence, pushing AI toward moral anti-realism. (7) Frontier labs (DeepMind, Anthropic) are institutionalizing philosophy via dedicated hires (Shevlin, Gabriel), but structural incentives favor speed over philosophical caution. The field is shifting from 'ontology as truth declaration' to 'ontology as disciplined semantic positioning' with meta-ontological governance.
